newsitem.title: ITALY: Olivetti to mull funds having board seat.
newsitem.headline: Olivetti to mull funds having board seat.

text.p: Troubled information and technology group Olivetti said on Monday it would consider any proposals from shareholding funds putting forward a possible candidate for a seat on the company's board.

Press reports have said mutual funds which own up to 70 percent of Olivetti might get a seat on its board and that a group of British fund managers had suggested to Olivetti's main shareholder CIR that a new independent member be appointed to Olivetti's executive committee.

The press reports said many U.K. investors with a stake in Olivetti had agreed on the person to represent them on the board and this was expected to be Dario Trevisan, an Italian lawyer who spoke for some U.K. funds at Olivetti's last shareholders' meeting in May.

The Olivetti spokeswoman said when was unable to comment on the press speculation but said "the board of directors and executive committee of Olivetti have told major shareholders that they are open to receive proposals on possible candidates in line with Olivetti's status as a public company."
Carlo De Benedetti's resignation as Olivetti chairman earlier this month after preliminary first half 1996 results showed larger than expected losses and debt caused major changes on the board.
Olivetti is due to publish its full first half report later today.
Members of the executive committee are Rodolfo De Benedetti, son of Carlo and CIR chief executive, Olivetti chairman Antonio Tesone, new CEO Roberto Colaninno and CIR executive Franco Girard.

De Benedetti's CIR industrial holding is the largest shareholder in Olivetti with a 14.7 percent stake. His COFIDE financial holding group last week announced it had bought 600,000 CIR shares bringing the holding of De Benedetti companies in CIR to 50.06 percent. -- Milan newsroom +392 66129589
